(a) the evolutionary approach is effective to solve the optimization problem of the design and optimum sizing of distributed information systems, (b) the evolutionary approach outperforms other conventional approaches in terms of costs, and (c) the evolutionary approach allows the designer to explore the design space, and to find a solution that is optimal for his/her specific problem.

(1) The proposed evolutionary design methodology can effectively be used to optimize the design of distributed information systems, by reducing costs and improving performance; (2) The proposed methodology is able to provide a significant cost reduction with respect to conventional design approaches.
the proposed methodology is capable of reducing costs by 10% to 20% in a typical IT architecture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an evolutionary approach for the optimization of distributed information systems.
the design of the distributed information system structure and the optimization of its cost.
the development of a new design approach to distributed IT architectures, which is based on the application of an evolutionary algorithm to the optimization problem of the physical system design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology is a valid and effective approach to the design and optimization of a distributed information system, which is a typical example of a complex system.
the proposed methodology is able to provide a significant contribution to the optimization of information systems design, in terms of cost reduction.
the proposed methodology is able to identify the optimal solution for the IT architecture design problem, with respect to a given set of requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed and implemented a methodology for the optimization of the distributed architecture of a client/server farm by applying genetic algorithms.
we have proposed a new methodology to optimize a complex system design, which is the design of a client/server-farm architecture.
the proposed methodology can be used to optimize the design and sizing of a distributed IT architecture by considering the whole system as an entity, rather than as a sum of its parts.

the proposed methodology is a valuable tool for IT designers, allowing them to explore the solution space of a distributed architecture, in order to select the best solution in a short amount of time, and to compare different solutions with respect to their costs and performances.
evolutionary algorithms can be successfully applied to the design of complex distributed IT architectures.
